Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 57, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Hadid (The Iron), because iron is mentioned in it in the context of divine blessing, and because of its great strength and its many benefits for people.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Reminding of God's majesty (jalal) and His great attributes, the vastness of His power and dominion, the comprehensiveness of His governance, and the breadth of His knowledge; commanding faith in God and in what His Messenger (ﷺ) brought; and urging spending in the way of God.

• Mention of what has been prepared for the believing men and women on the Day of Resurrection of good, and what has been prepared for the hypocritical men and women of punishment.

• Reminding of the Resurrection and clarifying the reality of the Hereafter; calling to abstinence (zuhd) from the transient, perishing life of this world; commanding patience in the face of calamities; and drawing attention to the wisdom behind the sending of messengers and the revelation of scriptures.

• Clarifying the similarity between the message of Muhammad (ﷺ) and the messages of Noah and Abraham (peace be upon them both) and those who came after them among the messengers, the last of whom was Jesus, since they were all sent with the law of Islam. Among those nations some were guided, and some were defiant, disobedient to obedience. Likewise, the nation of the Prophet (ﷺ) includes believers and disbelievers; and it calls people to the fear of God (taqwa) and to faith in His Messenger, and to the reward God has prepared for them for that.

[Tafsir]

Everything in the heavens and the earth, of all His creatures, glorifies God and declares Him free of any imperfection, and He is the Mighty over His creation, the Wise in managing their affairs.

His is the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them. He is the Owner who disposes of His creation: He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things Capable. Nothing He wills is beyond His power; whatever He wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be.

He is the First, before whom nothing existed, and the Last, after whom nothing will exist; the Outward, above whom nothing is, and the Inward, nearer than whom nothing is. Nothing is hidden from Him on earth or in the heavens, and He has knowledge of all things.

He is the One who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days. Then He rose over the Throne (istawa), that is, He ascended and was elevated above all His creation, in a manner that befits His majesty. He knows what enters the earth of seeds and rain and other things, what comes out of it of plants, crops and fruits, what descends from the sky of rain and other things, and what ascends into it of angels and deeds. He, glorified is He, is with you by His knowledge wherever you are, and Allah is Seeing of your deeds that you do, and He will recompense you for them.
He has the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah is the return of all creatures' affairs in the Hereafter; He will recompense them for their deeds.

He causes what is lost from the hours of the night to enter into the day, so the day lengthens, and He causes what is lost from the hours of the day to enter into the night, so the night lengthens. And He, glorified is He, is All-Knowing of what is concealed within hearts and what breasts harbor; nothing of that is hidden from Him.

Believe in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and spend from what Allah has provided you of wealth and has made you its trustees. So those of you, O people, who believe and spend from their wealth will have a great reward.

What excuse do you have for not believing in the oneness of Allah and acting by His law, when the Messenger calls you to that, and Allah has already taken your covenant on it, if you are believers in Allah your Creator?

He is the One who sends down to His servant Muhammad (ﷺ) clear, distinct verses from the Qur'an, in order to bring you out by them from the darkness of disbelief into the light of faith. Indeed, Allah, in bringing you out from the darkness into the light, is most merciful to you with a vast mercy, in your present life and in your hereafter, and He will reward you with the best of rewards.

Why should you not spend in the cause of God? To God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth; He inherits everything in them, and no one remains owning anything in them. Those among you who spent and fought before the conquest of Makkah (Mecca) are not equal in reward and recompense to those who spent and fought after it. Those [who spent before the conquest] are greater in rank with God than those who spent in the cause of God after the conquest and fought the disbelievers. Yet God has promised Paradise to each of the two groups. And God is Aware of what you do; nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He will reward you for it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 57, verse 11:

Who is it that will lend to Allah a good loan, spending in the way of Allah seeking reward from Him with a sincere heart, without reminding of favor or causing harm, so that his Lord will multiply for him the reward and recompense, and he will have a noble reward, which is Paradise?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 57, verse 12:

On the day you see the believing men and the believing women, their light running before them and on their right, according to their deeds. It will be said to them: "Good news for you today: entry into spacious gardens, from beneath whose palaces and trees the rivers flow. You will never leave them. That is the great triumph for you in the Hereafter."

On the Day when the hypocrite men and hypocrite women will say to the believers, "Wait for us, that we may borrow some of your light!" It will be said to them, mocking them: "Turn back behind you and seek light!" Then a wall with a gate will be set between them: its inner side, facing the believers, will contain mercy, and its outer side, facing the hypocrites, will contain punishment.

The hypocrites will call out to the believers, saying: "Were we not with you in the world, performing the rites of religion just as you did?" The believers will say to them: "Yes, you were with us outwardly, but you ruined yourselves through hypocrisy and sins. You waited for misfortunes to befall the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers, you doubted the Resurrection after death, your false desires deceived you, and you remained upon that until death came to you, and Satan deceived you about Allah."

Today no compensation will be accepted from any of you, O hypocrites, that you might ransom yourselves from the punishment of Allah, nor from those who disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger. Your destination, all of you, is the Fire; it is more fitting for you than any other abode, and wretched is that destination.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 57, verse 16:

Has the time not come for those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and who follow His guidance, that their hearts should be humbled at the remembrance of Allah and at hearing the Qur'an, and that they should not be like those who were given the Scripture before them, [namely] the Jews and Christians, who, when the time lengthened upon them, altered the words of Allah, so their hearts became hard, and many of them are defiant of obedience to Allah?

In the verse is an exhortation to tenderness of heart and humility before Allah, the Exalted, when hearing what He has sent down of the Book and the wisdom, and a warning against resembling the Jews and Christians in the hardness of their hearts and their departure from obedience to Allah.

Know that Allah, glory be to Him, gives life to the earth with rain after its death, so it brings forth vegetation. Likewise, Allah is able to bring the dead back to life on the Day of Resurrection, and He is the One who is able to soften hearts after their hardness. We have made clear to you the signs of Our power, so that perhaps you will understand them and be admonished.

Indeed, the men and women who give charity from their wealth, and who spend in the way of Allah generous spending that they give willingly, seeking the Face of Allah, will have their reward multiplied for them. And besides that, they will have a great reward, which is Paradise.

Those who have believed in Allah and His messengers and have not made distinction between any of them—those are the ṣiddīqūn (the truthful ones, those whose affirmation is complete), who have fully affirmed what the messengers brought, in belief, speech, and action. And the martyrs (shuhadā') are with their Lord; for them is their great reward with Allah and their great light on the Day of Resurrection. As for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and proofs, those are the companions of Hellfire; for them there is no reward and no light.

Know, O people, that the life of this world is nothing but play and amusement: bodies play with it, and hearts are diverted by it; it is an adornment you beautify yourselves with, a source of boasting among you over its goods, and a competition in numbers of wealth and children. Its likeness is that of rain whose vegetation pleases the farmers; then it dries up, so you see it turn yellow after its greenness, then it becomes crushed, dry debris. In the Hereafter there is severe punishment for the disbelievers, and forgiveness from Allah and His pleasure for the people of faith. And the life of this world, for one who works for it while forgetting his Hereafter, is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.

Compete with one another, O people, in striving toward the means of forgiveness: sincere repentance and abstaining from sins, so that you may be granted forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose breadth is like the breadth of the heaven and the earth. It has been prepared for those who believe in the oneness of Allah and follow His messengers. ﴿That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills of His creation.﴾ Entrance into Paradise is not attained except by the mercy of Allah and His bounty, together with righteous deeds. Allah is the Possessor of great kindness and abundant, all-encompassing giving toward His believing servants.

This is the commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 57, verse 22:

Whatever calamity befalls you, O people, either on the earth or in your own selves, such as sicknesses, hunger, and afflictions, is already written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) before the creation comes into being. Indeed, that is easy for Allah, the Exalted.

So that you do not grieve over what has escaped you of worldly things, nor exult in what He has given you with the exultation of arrogance and conceit. Indeed, Allah does not love every arrogant boaster, who is proud of what he has been given of worldly goods and boasts over others with it. These arrogant people are those who are stingy with their wealth, not spending it in the way of Allah, and who command people to be stingy, adorning it for them. And whoever turns away from the obedience of Allah harms only himself, and he will never harm Allah in the least, for Allah is the Self-Sufficient above His creation, the Praiseworthy, who possesses every complete and beautiful attribute and every beautiful act that deserves to be praised.

So that you do not grieve over what has escaped you of worldly things, nor exult in what He has given you with the exultation of arrogance and conceit. Indeed, Allah does not love every arrogant boaster, who is proud of what he has been given of worldly goods and boasts over others with it. These arrogant people are those who are stingy with their wealth, not spending it in the way of Allah, and who command people to be stingy, adorning it for them. And whoever turns away from the obedience of Allah harms only himself, and he will never harm Allah in the least, for Allah is the Self-Sufficient above His creation, the Praiseworthy, who possesses every complete and beautiful attribute and every beautiful act that deserves to be praised.

We sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and sent down with them the Book containing the rulings and laws, and sent down the Balance, so that people would deal with one another justly. And We sent down iron, in which there is great strength and many benefits for people, and so that Allah would make manifest to His creation who supports His religion and His messengers in the unseen. Indeed, Allah is Strong, not overcome, Mighty, not defeated.

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 57, verse 26:**

And We certainly sent Noah and Abraham, and We placed in their descendants prophethood and the revealed Scriptures. Among them is one who is guided to the truth, but many of them are deviators from the obedience of Allah.

Then We sent, following in their footsteps, Our messengers, and We sent Noah and Abraham before them, and We placed prophethood and the Book among their descendants. Then We followed them with Our messengers, whom We sent with clear proofs, and We sent after them Jesus, son of Mary, and We gave him the Injeel (Gospel), and We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy. They were affectionate toward one another, but they invented monasticism (ruhbaniyyah) through excessive devotion in worship, which We had not prescribed for them. Rather, they themselves committed to it on their own initiative, intending thereby to seek the pleasure of Allah. But they did not observe it with its due observance. So We gave those among them who believed in Allah and His messengers their reward in proportion to their faith, but many of them are defiant of Allah's obedience and deniers of His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ).

O you who believe, carry out Allah's commands and avoid His prohibitions, and believe in His Messenger. He will give you a double portion of His mercy, appoint for you a light by which you will be guided, and forgive your sins. Allah is Oft-Forgiving to His servants and Most Merciful to them.

God has given you all of that, so that the People of the Scripture who have not believed in Muhammad (ﷺ) may know that they have no power over any of God's bounty, to earn it for themselves or to bestow it on others, and that all bounty is in the hand of God alone, who gives it to whomever He wills of His servants. And God is the Possessor of great kindness and abundant, far-reaching giving toward His creation.
